question_title: How many locally acquired human West Nile virus cases will ECDC report for Italy in the 2026 season by the surveillance report published around 7 August 2026?
summary: Italy cumulative locally-acquired human WNV cases in the ECDC report published on/around 7 Aug 2026. Current: 46 through 22 July (Week 30). The 2025 season is a strong, directly comparable analog: at the equivalent date 2025 had 32 cases and grew to 173 two weeks later (increments +57, +84). 2026's latest weekly increment (20→46 = +26, from the question description) nearly matches 2025's +27, and 2026 starts from a higher base (46 vs 32). Calendar-verified that Aug 7 2026 is a Friday when the Week 32 report (data through Wed Aug 5, two increments) publishes — matching the author's explicit expectation. Monte Carlo mixture: 80% Week-32 two-increment scenario (2025-calibrated growth factors ~2.0× then ~1.5×, season multiplier, Poisson dispersion; median ~180) + 20% Week-31 one-increment scenario (publication-timing risk; ~90–115). Result: median 163, mean 173, with a lower shoulder from timing risk and a right-skewed upper tail (proportional-lead hot scenario ~230–250). Open upper bound; P(>350)~1.9%.

factors.description: 2025 Italy analog: comparable-date cumulative 32 (Jul23) grew to 173 (Aug6) in two weeks (increments +57,+84). 2026's last increment +26 nearly matches 2025's +27, from a higher base (46 vs 32). Under Week-32 (two-increment) this anchors ~180.
Italian WNV season peaks in August; early-Aug is squarely in the rising phase, so weekly increments almost certainly keep growing.
Report-timing risk: ~20% chance the governing report is Week 31 (one increment, ~90-115) rather than Week 32, given the 00:00 UTC Aug-7 resolve timestamp vs same-day Friday publication.
2026 running ahead of 2025 on cumulative could push a proportional-lead hot scenario toward 230-250 (upper tail).

resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the cumulative number of locally acquired (autochthonous) human West Nile virus infections reported for Italy in the 2026 transmission season, as shown in the ECDC weekly seasonal surveillance report for humans found at https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/west-nile-fever/surveillance-and-disease-data/disease-data-ecdc . Specifically, it resolves to the total number of human cases listed for Italy (summing all Italian NUTS3/affected areas) in the most recent weekly report published on or before 7 August 2026 — expected to be the Week 32 report covering data through approximately 5 August 2026. For example, if the report shows Italy with 120 locally acquired human cases, this resolves as 120. If ECDC does not publish a new report between 24 July and 7 August 2026, the most recent available report as of 7 August 2026 is used; if the ECDC page is permanently unavailable and the figure cannot be recovered from ECDC materials or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), the question is annulled.
fine_print: Only locally acquired (autochthonous) human cases counted by ECDC for Italy are included; travel-associated/imported cases are excluded. Figures are preliminary and may be revised; the value shown in the applicable report governs, even if later revised.

revision_history.reviewer_assessment:
I verified the factors against the research trace (session 44864) and worldview research. Two compounding errors push the agent's center (174) materially too high; I estimate the center should be roughly 120–135.

**1. Report-timing error — the dominant flaw (drives the fail).** The question resolves at 2026-08-07T00:00:00Z using "the most recent weekly report published on or before 7 August." The agent's OWN research (trace lines 889–894, 1044) establishes that ECDC publishes WNV reports every FRIDAY: Week 30 (data as at Tue 22 Jul) posted Fri 25 Jul; Week 31 (data ~29 Jul) ~Fri 31 Jul/1 Aug; Week 32 (data ~5 Aug) would post Friday 7 August. But the resolution timestamp is 00:00 UTC on Friday 7 August — the very start of the day, before that Friday's report would post. So the governing report is very likely Week 31 (data through ~29 Jul), reflecting only ONE increment past the current 46, not the two increments the agent's base case assumes. The agent assigned this "one increment" outcome only 8% weight (execute_code line 1106: `mask = random < 0.08`), treating Week 32 as the near-certain base. That is backwards: the single-increment (Week 31) scenario deserves majority weight. A one-increment forecast lands around 46 + a rising-phase increment (~+50–70 per the 2025 analog, or +26 raw) ≈ 75–115. With most mass there, the center should sit near 120–135, not 174. The resolution text says "expected to be the Week 32 report," but it is explicitly conditioned on "published on or before 7 August," and the agent's own Friday-publication schedule makes Week 31 the more probable governing report. This is a resolution-misalignment/timing error that the agent under-weighted by roughly an order of magnitude.

**2. Fabricated 2026 trajectory / "+26" increment (soft hallucination).** Factor 1's headline claim — "2026's last weekly increment (+26) nearly matches 2025's (+27)" — and the Monte Carlo's `inc_last=26.0` rest on a prior-week 2026 value (code comment "Jul15 cum ~20", trace line 1058) that appears in NO source. The research trace and worldview research (ecdc-...-2ba53907.json) contain exactly ONE 2026 data point: Italy = 46 as at 22 July (Week 30). The invented series "Jun24:2, Jul1:3, Jul15:~20, Jul22:46" is the agent's own construction. The rising-phase base of 46 is well-grounded, so this doesn't flip direction, but it manufactures false precision in the central "2026 tracks 2025" claim and helps prop up the high center. On its own this is a warn; combined with Issue 1 it reinforces the overstatement.

**Other notes.** Tool-audit claim "No tool failures" is consistent with ground truth (0 errors). The 2025 analog data (32→89→173, increments +57/+84) is well-sourced from ISS bollettini and ECDC — not fabricated. The counterargument is genuinely strong (it correctly identifies the Week 31-vs-32 timing risk, the ISS-vs-ECDC proxy risk, and the Lazio-focus caveat, and even self-estimates 130–150) and confidence_in_estimate=0.50 is appropriately humble — but the agent then did NOT fold that timing insight into its point estimate, leaving the 8% weighting and 174 center unchanged. Because the agent's own adversarial analysis reached the right lower range (130–150) and then failed to act on it, the published center is meaningfully miscalibrated upward.

**Recommended center: ~120–135**, with a wider and lower-skewed distribution reflecting the majority probability that only Week 31 (one increment) governs at resolution.

1. Factor 1 (2025 analog) — GROUNDED. The 2025 ISS series (23 Jul=32, 30 Jul=89, 6 Aug=173; increments +57, +84) is confirmed in the trace via TravelHealthPro/ISS/ANSA cross-validation (lines 45, 287, 292; reconciled a NaTHNaC mislabeling). The ISS-as-ECDC-proxy assumption is sound and explicitly justified (virtually all Italian cases are autochthonous; ECDC season total of 779 = locally acquired).

2. 2026 anchor (46 cases through 22 July) — INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The live ECDC Week 30 report and the fresh worldview research entry (ecdc-...-2ba53907, state=fresh) both confirm Italy=46 as at 22 July 2026. This is the value that actually drives the forecast base.

3. The "2->3->20->46" intermediate trajectory — Only the endpoint (46, verified) and the last increment (~26) feed the MC. The intermediate values 2, 3, 20 do not appear anywhere in the research trace, but the agent attributes them to the question description, and they don't move the forecast. Since the core claim (base=46) is verified and 46 > 2025's 32 supports the "higher base" reasoning, this is at most a minor traceability gap, not a hallucination of a load-bearing claim.

4. Report-timing (Factor 3) — Legitimate and well-handled. Calendar verified via execute_code (Aug 7 2026 = Friday; Week 32 data-through Aug 5 = Wednesday). The 00:00 UTC Aug-7 resolve timestamp genuinely creates ambiguity about whether Week 31 or Week 32 governs; the agent raised the Week-31 weight from 8% to 20% after premortem and respects the author's explicit "expected Week 32" statement. Defensible.

5. Factor signs — All consistent with descriptions. Factor 3 correctly carries the negative (timing discount) logit; Factors 1/2/4 positive.

6. Double-counting — Factors 1, 2, 4 all lean on the 2025 analog, but they function as scenario point-estimates feeding a single Monte Carlo mixture, not as independent multiplicative logits, so this is coherent rather than double-counting.

7. Tool audit — The agent does not claim "no tool failures." The premortem tool's 100% error rate (1 call) reflects the tool erroring, not a contradiction of the agent's narrative about research quality. No misrepresentation of the metrics.

INDEPENDENT PROBABILITY VIEW: The two-increment base case (median ~180, matching the 46+55+82=183 analog point estimate) is well-calibrated. The one upward-bias risk is the season multiplier (median 1.05) tilting hotter when 2025 was a record year potentially not repeating — but 2026 running ahead on cumulative (46 vs 32) partially offsets this, and the 20% timing discount pulls the center down. My own estimate lands ~155-175, essentially aligned with the agent's 163 center. The distribution shape (P10~96, P50~163, P90~262, open upper tail, P(>350)~1.9%) is reasonable.

Confidence of 0.50 is appropriately humble given the real report-timing ambiguity and single-season analog. No overconfidence.
